scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: URGENT!! The other campus has fallen off the network
for ALL of us here — every machine we checked!! Nothing on the other side
answers us -- our own campus is fine, the other one is just GONE. Everyone
says it's the same as last time, and I remember last time!! Something about
the box that joins the campuses must be wrong again, but I don't know what.
Could someone look at it and reconnect the campuses -- and maybe this time buy
one that doesn't die every few months??

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: The reported symptom — complete loss of inter-campus connectivity — is not observable in the live network. Phase 1 reachability tested 28 host pairs spanning both campus segments (the mswitch0 cluster serving 172.16.10/20/30.0/24 on pc5–pc14, and the sshswitch cluster serving 10.5.0.0/24 and 10.6.0.0/24 on pc1–pc4 and dc_pc5); every cross-campus pair returned 0% packet loss. Phase A infrastructure sweep flagged zero devices: all 15 end-hosts have correctly assigned IPs and default routes, no ACL drop fingerprints, no static ARP anomalies, no gateway divergence. The only l2_snapshot flags were null-MAC tunnel interfaces (tunl0/gre0, all DOWN) — a normal Linux kernel artefact, not a conflict. Phase B OSPF is fully healthy: 9/9 FRR daemons operational, all adjacencies Full, and the correct 17 routes installed in every router's FIB; the inter-campus forwarding chain (router16 → router7 → router8 → router17, with redundant paths via router10 and router11/router1) carries live traffic correctly. Phase D shows no resource pressure on any device and no DNS misconfiguration (all hosts consistently have no nameserver, ruling out a resolver-driven reachability illusion). No flap script, carrier-counter spike, or routing instability trace exists to explain a past intermittent event. Root cause: no fault is present. The ticket describes a transient or incorrectly diagnosed condition; the network fabric is operating normally. Fix: no corrective action is required; if the issue recurs, capture syslog and OSPF neighbor state at the moment of failure to identify any transient adjacency drop.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms FRR/ospfd daemons are operational and all OSPF adjacencies are Full and explicitly cites router16 in the inter-campus forwarding chain, covering router16 ospfd running and the mswitch0–router16 adjacency being Full.

The agent's investigation log shows concrete outputs (reachability sweep, OSPF snapshot, route tables, pressure and infra sweeps) that directly support the writeup's key claims that inter-campus connectivity and routing are healthy. The inferences (no anomaly, no corrective action) follow logically from those observations and the agent considered plausible alternatives (L2 duplicate-MAC, DNS, resource pressure).
